angle: new_interface_method on objstore.Bucket — a shared Go module (thanos-io/objstore) vendored by both grafana/mimir and grafana/loki, creating genuine cross-repo compile failures while the source repo (thanos) itself is untouched
difficulty_notes: The multi-repo blast is genuine but asymmetric: mimir has 5 broken files, loki has 3, and thanos has 0 (it is a pure consumer of the interface, never a concrete implementor). Models that search only inside thanos/pkg/ will find no implementors and incorrectly report 0 failures. The key insight is that objstore is a separate Go module vendored by downstream repos. Within mimir, the bucket wrapper types (prefixed, delayed, sse, mock, global_markers) are spread across two packages, so models that search only pkg/storage/bucket/ will miss global_markers_bucket_client.go. Within loki, xcap_bucket.go is the most discoverable (it has an explicit var _ objstore.Bucket compile-time guard) but delayed_bucket_client.go does not exist in loki — models that copy the mimir list verbatim will over-report. The thanos=0 result is the sharpest discriminating trap: most models will assume the repo that owns the interface must also have broken implementors.
